title: Rebuild your data structures foundation
description: Review core structures with short examples, memory diagrams, and quick checks before returning to graded work.

title: Trace algorithms visually
description: Practice following stack, queue, tree, and graph operations step by step to expose gaps in your reasoning.

title: Complexity analysis workshop
description: Compare common implementations and explain how input size changes their runtime and memory costs.

title: Advanced graph problems
description: Stretch your skills with weighted paths, traversal tradeoffs, and a compact real-world graph challenge.

title: Semantic HTML refresher
description: Revisit document structure, accessible labels, and browser behavior through small corrective examples.

title: React state practice
description: Work through focused component-state exercises and identify when data should be derived instead of stored.

title: Accessibility debugging lab
description: Inspect a small interface, diagnose keyboard and screen-reader issues, and propose targeted fixes.

title: Web performance patterns
description: Explore rendering, loading, and caching tradeoffs through an advanced front-end optimization challenge.

title: Data cleaning essentials
description: Practice identifying missing values, inconsistent categories, and outliers in a guided dataset.

title: Exploratory analysis practice
description: Choose useful summaries and visualizations, then explain the patterns and limitations you find.

title: Model evaluation lab
description: Compare metrics, check validation results, and decide which model best fits a practical scenario.

title: Feature engineering challenge
description: Create and defend new features for a noisy dataset, then test whether they improve a model.

title: User research foundations
description: Review unbiased questions, observation notes, and evidence-based findings with a guided example.

title: Journey mapping practice
description: Turn research notes into a focused journey map that connects user needs to design opportunities.

title: Usability diagnosis lab
description: Evaluate a prototype, prioritize observed friction, and recommend changes tied to user evidence.

title: Design systems prototype
description: Build an advanced component pattern that balances consistency, accessibility, and product context.

title: 15-minute study plan reset
description: Turn unfinished work into a realistic sequence of small study blocks with a clear first task.

title: Build a spaced-practice routine
description: Plan three short retrieval sessions that reinforce weak material without creating a last-minute crunch.

title: Cross-course transfer challenge
description: Apply a strong concept from one course to a new problem and reflect on what transfers successfully.

title: Peer-teaching extension
description: Create a concise explanation or worked example that could help a classmate master a difficult idea.
